1. Introduction                                                    actions from inputs. This omission undermines manipulation
Recent years have witnessed significant progress in general-       interpretability and limits their performance on long-horizon,
purpose robotic manipulation policies [4, 5, 18, 25, 31, 41,       complex tasks that require structured planning.
58]. Among these advances, VLA models have emerged as                 Inspired by the chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning [1, 44]
a powerful paradigm by leveraging the multimodal under-            in large language models (LLMs), wherein complex prob-
standing of pre-trained Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to           lems are decomposed into intermediate steps through prompt-
enhance embodied generalization [2, 6, 14, 18, 19, 29, 58].        ing, thereby enhancing reasoning performance. In robotics,
By fine-tuning on robot interaction data, VLA models inherit       integrating CoT holds promise for grounding reasoning in
open-world reasoning capabilities from VLMs [3, 16], map-          textual instructions, visual observations, and actions. Prior

Figure 2. Overview of the proposed TRM-VLA (Sec. 3.2). (a) System design: VLM backbone for reasoning and diffusion expert for
execution. (b) Keyframe-Triggered Reasoning (Sec. 3.3) performs hierarchical reasoning only at critical frames supervised by temporal
reasoning data. (c) Granularity-adaptable Context Memory (Sec. 3.4) maintains a dynamic memory buffer to enhance inter-frame reasoning
coherence.

serve as a direct proxy for computational cost. As shown in            5. Conclusion
Tab. 1, our TRM-VLA achieves superior efficiency: it gener-           We present TRM-VLA, a novel Vision-Language-Action
ates only 4.3 tokens per step, a dramatic reduction compared          framework that integrates temporal-aware reasoning and ex-
to prior reasoning-augmented models. For instance, while              plicit memory into robotic policy learning. By triggering
ECoT (the reasoning version of OpenVLA) improves the                  hierarchical chain-of-thought reasoning only at critical deci-
success rate over its base model, it incurs a 3.8x increase in        sion points and dynamically maintaining a structured mem-
token generation (7.0 vs. 26.8). Similarly, CogACT-ECoT               ory of past reasoning traces, TRM-VLA achieves strong per-
builds upon CogACT-Base but increases the tokens from                 formance on long-horizon, memory-intensive manipulation
1.0 to 26.3. In contrast, TRM-VLA achieves a trade-off                tasks while drastically reducing computational overhead. Ex-
between performance and efficiency. This efficiency stems             tensive experiments across simulated and real-world bench-
from our design principle of triggering reasoning only at             marks demonstrate that our method sets new state-of-the-art
critical frames, thereby avoiding redundant computation.              results in both success rate and inference efficiency. We hope
Effectiveness of KTR and GCM. As shown in Tab. 4 and                  TRM-VLA will serve as a foundation for future work on
Tab. 5, both KTR and GCM modules are essential. On the                temporally grounded, memory-augmented agents that reason
SIMPLER, removing either KTR (ID a) or GCM (ID c)                     strategically and act efficiently in complex environments.
